speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This is particularly relevant for smaller players or emerging media businesses that may grow in the regulated space over time.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Where smaller players or emerging players fall in the regulated space, will IMDA also adopt a proportionate approach to compliance?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Will there be clear guidelines for simple processes or differentiated expectation between large incumbents and smaller entrants?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I raise this because competition regulation should not prevent unfair dominance alone.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It should also preserve innovation, entry and space for new players to grow.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In plain English, we should not protect competition in a way which makes it harder for future competitors to emerge.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: My second point is on Singapore's relevance and investability.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Singapore's strength has always been not just only stable, but we are clear, predictable and trusted.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And these are important reasons why investors choose to invest here.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And investability is not an abstract concept because when companies invest in Singapore, they bring capital, they bring capabilities, regional functions and jobs.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: They create opportunities not just for senior executives but also Singaporeans working in content, marketing, production, communication and many other roles.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: You see, investors and business do not expect a market to be unregulated.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It tells serious players the following things: one, the rules here in Singapore are fair; two, that dominant players cannot abuse their position; and three, that the system will not allow unfair concentration of control.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In this regard, this Bill sends a positive signal.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This is sensible because media ownership is not just commercial matters, because it affects competition, consumer interest and public trust.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: See, at the same time, the powers introduced in this Bill are significant.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The Bill strengthens control over ownership and effective control.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It allows IMDA to issue directions in relations to regulated person and essential resources.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It provides a stronger intervention where competition or the public interest is at stake.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But precisely because such powers are significant, the basis for exercising them should be clear.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: So, I would like to ask how the Government intends to provide clarity on key concepts, such as public interest, effective control, substantial leasing of competition and essential resources?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Will IMDA also publish clear decision frameworks or guidelines on how these concepts will be applied?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Will businesses and investors be given sufficient clarity on the types of transactions or conduct that may raise such concerns?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This is important because investors are not just asking whether this system is fair.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: They are also asking whether this system is predictable.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: A system can be interventionistic, if needed or when needed, but if the basis for intervention is not well understood, investors may hesitate.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I also note that the Bill provides for reconsideration request to IMDA and appeals to the Minister.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But could the Minister also clarify how does this safeguard works in practice?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Strong regulatory power should match with strong clarity.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This is how we preserve Singapore's reputation as a place where markets are well-governed, trusted and investable.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: My final point is on outcomes for consumers and our residents.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The Bill seeks to promote competition in the media industry.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In this principle, this should lead to more choices, better services, fairer access and greater innovation.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But from the perspective of the ordinary resident, the issue is not really how many media companies exist.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The issue is whether the media environment, whether what they experience is diverse, reliable, accessible and trustworthy.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: A person may have access to many sources but still see a narrow slice of content.
